<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Stochastic Interest Rates</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this appendix, we relax Assumption <a href="#Thmassumption1" title="Assumption 1. ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and examine how stochastic interest rates change our analysis. We first show that the payoff to the arbitrage strategies changes by exactly one term: a rebalancing cash flow from changes in hedge ratios. Because the hedge ratio tracks interest rates, this term introduces additional interest rate risk.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We then ask how large instantaneous interest rate changes would have to be to rationalize the deviations we observe. We find empirically that the implied interest rate changes turn out to be one to two orders of magnitude larger than any observed movement in interest rates. This suggests stochastic interest rate risk is unlikely to account for the observed deviations of perpetual futures from the benchmark.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">When the interest rate is stochastic, define the discount factor as</p>
<table id="A6.E60" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E60.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="D_{t}=\exp\left(-\int_{0}^{t}r_{s}ds\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}=\exp\left(-\int_{0}^{t}r_{s}ds\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(60)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.p3.2" class="ltx_p">A stochastic rate affects the arbitrage strategies of Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> through two channels. First, the hedging ratio of Corollary <a href="#Thmcorollary2" title="Corollary 2 (No-arbitrage price for Binance). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> depends on the interest rate, so the arbitrageur must adjust her spot holdings as the rate moves. Second, financing, reinvestment, and discounting run at the prevailing rate <math id="A6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Mirroring the proof of Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition2" title="Proposition 2 (No-arbitrage price: Edge Case). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, for each strategy in Table <a href="#A6.T1" title="Table F.1 ‣ Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a>, we consider a hedge ratio tailored to its own side of the benchmark:</p>
<table id="A6.E61" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E61.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\lambda}(r)\equiv\frac{\kappa}{\kappa-\gamma-r}\quad\text{for the first strategy},\qquad\underline{\lambda}(r)\equiv\frac{\kappa}{\kappa+\gamma-r}\quad\text{for the second}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>for the first strategy</mtext><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>for the second</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}(r)\equiv\frac{\kappa}{\kappa-\gamma-r}\quad\text{for the first strategy},\qquad\underline{\lambda}(r)\equiv\frac{\kappa}{\kappa+\gamma-r}\quad\text{for the second}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(61)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.p4.2" class="ltx_p">The two expressions extend the two branches of the proportionality constant in Corollary <a href="#Thmcorollary2" title="Corollary 2 (No-arbitrage price for Binance). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> across all interest rate levels: <math id="A6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\lambda}(r)=\lambda(r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}(r)=\lambda(r)</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>ι</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;\iota</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\lambda}(r)=\lambda(r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\lambda}(r)=\lambda(r)</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&lt;\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ι</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&lt;\iota</annotation></semantics></math>. The advantage of this choice is smoothness: whereas <math id="A6.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(r)</annotation></semantics></math> switches branches discretely when the rate crosses <math id="A6.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ι</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\iota</annotation></semantics></math>, each of <math id="A6.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><munder accentunder="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> varies continuously with the rate, so tracking the hedge never requires a discrete jump in position.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T1" title="Table F.1 ‣ Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a> presents the cash flows of the two strategies with a rate-contingent hedge ratio <math id="A6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, equal to <math id="A6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\lambda}(r_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}(r_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> for the first strategy and to <math id="A6.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\lambda}(r_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\lambda}(r_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> for the second. Relative to Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, there is one new row: over each interval, the first strategy purchases <math id="A6.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\lambda_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\lambda_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> units of spot at price <math id="A6.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> to keep the hedge matched to the prevailing rate, a rebalancing cash flow of <math id="A6.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-S_{s}d\lambda_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-S_{s}d\lambda_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> financed through the money market account.</p>
</div>

For interest rate paths of finite variation, the product rule contains no covariation term, <math id="A6.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\left(\lambda_{s}S_{s}\right)=\lambda_{s}dS_{s}+S_{s}d\lambda_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\left(\lambda_{s}S_{s}\right)=\lambda_{s}dS_{s}+S_{s}d\lambda_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. <p id="A6.p6.3" class="ltx_p">Defining the deviation relative to the strategy’s hedge, <math id="A6.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{s}\equiv F_{s}-\lambda_{s}S_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{s}\equiv F_{s}-\lambda_{s}S_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, substituting <math id="A6.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-dF_{s}+\lambda_{s}dS_{s}=-du_{s}-S_{s}d\lambda_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-dF_{s}+\lambda_{s}dS_{s}=-du_{s}-S_{s}d\lambda_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, and integrating by parts, we obtain</p>

<p id="A6.p6.4" class="ltx_p">The payoff of the second strategy is the negative of the same expression with <math id="A6.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{s}=\underline{\lambda}(r_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{s}=\underline{\lambda}(r_{s})</annotation></semantics></math>. When the short rate is constant, <math id="A6.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\lambda_{s}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\lambda_{s}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the hedge ratio of the profitable side coincides with the proportionality constant of Corollary <a href="#Thmcorollary2" title="Corollary 2 (No-arbitrage price for Binance). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, and Equation (<a href="#A6.E64" title="In Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">64</span></a>) reduces to the constant-rate payoff underlying Inequality (<a href="#S3.E5" title="In 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The first three terms of Equation (<a href="#A6.E64" title="In Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">64</span></a>) are the familiar components of the constant-rate payoff: the initial deviation, the discounted deviation at unwinding, and the present value of accumulated funding payments net of financing costs. Whenever the first strategy’s position is open, <math id="A6.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{s}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{s}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, the premium index lies above the point at which the funding rate equals the prevailing interest rate, so <math id="A6.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi(p_{s})&gt;r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi(p_{s})&gt;r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and the funding flow is positive; the second strategy is symmetric.<span id="footnote17" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">17</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">17</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">17</span>
            
            
            
          For the first strategy, <math id="footnote17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{s}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{s}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is equivalent to <math id="footnote17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{F_{s}-S_{s}}{F_{s}}&gt;\frac{r_{s}+\gamma}{\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>&gt;</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mi>κ</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{F_{s}-S_{s}}{F_{s}}&gt;\frac{r_{s}+\gamma}{\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math>, the root of <math id="footnote17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi(p_{s})=r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi(p_{s})=r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> on the upper linear branch of the funding rate function. When <math id="footnote17.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}\geq\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mi>ι</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}\geq\iota</annotation></semantics></math>, the premium index then lies on the upper branch above this root, so <math id="footnote17.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi(p_{s})=\kappa\frac{F_{s}-S_{s}}{F_{s}}-\gamma&gt;r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi(p_{s})=\kappa\frac{F_{s}-S_{s}}{F_{s}}-\gamma&gt;r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="footnote17.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}&lt;\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ι</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}&lt;\iota</annotation></semantics></math>, the premium index lies above the lower edge of the clamp region (because <math id="footnote17.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\gamma&gt;\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>ι</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\gamma&gt;\iota</annotation></semantics></math>), so <math id="footnote17.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi(p_{s})\geq\iota&gt;r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>ι</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi(p_{s})\geq\iota&gt;r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. The verification for the second strategy is symmetric.</span></span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p8.1" class="ltx_p">The genuinely new term is the rebalancing cash flow <math id="A6.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{0}^{t}D_{s}S_{s}d\lambda_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{0}^{t}D_{s}S_{s}d\lambda_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>: the arbitrageur adjusts a full spot notional as the rate moves her hedge ratio. The rebalancing term is closely related to changes in the interest rate. Because the hedge ratios in Equation (<a href="#A6.E61" title="In Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">61</span></a>) are smooth in the rate, <math id="A6.p8.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="d\lambda_{s}=\overline{\lambda}{}^{\prime}(r_{s})\,dr_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mmultiscripts><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mprescripts></mprescripts><mrow></mrow><mo>′</mo></mmultiscripts><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\lambda_{s}=\overline{\lambda}{}^{\prime}(r_{s})\,dr_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A6.p8.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\overline{\lambda}{}^{\prime}(r)=\kappa/\left(\kappa-\gamma-r\right)^{2}\approx 1/\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mmultiscripts><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mprescripts></mprescripts><mrow></mrow><mo>′</mo></mmultiscripts><mo>=</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\lambda}{}^{\prime}(r)=\kappa/\left(\kappa-\gamma-r\right)^{2}\approx 1/\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, and the term can be approximated by:</p>
<table id="A6.E65" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A6.p8.2" class="ltx_p">the analogous expression holding for <math id="A6.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><munder accentunder="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math>. We can understand this term as the discounted notional amount times the changes in interest rate. Since the interest rate, like the funding parameters, is measured per funding interval, a cumulative movement of one percentage point in the annualized interest rate over the life of a trade costs the arbitrageur at most about <math id="A6.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> basis point of spot notional.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Based on this framework, we then quantify the empirical relevance of interest rate risk for our results. We ask how large an instantaneous interest rate change would have to be to rationalize the deviations we observe.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p10.1" class="ltx_p">The proof of Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (No-arbitrage price: General Case). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows that the fundamental price is pinned down by the condition that the funding rate equals the risk-free rate, <math id="A6.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi(p_{t})=r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi(p_{t})=r</annotation></semantics></math>. Inverting this condition at observed prices defines the implied interest rate</p>

</div>

<p id="A6.p11.3" class="ltx_p">This is exactly the payoff to the arbitrage strategy with the initial deviation defined by the new rate <math id="A6.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. </div>
<div id="A6.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p12.1" class="ltx_p">The difference <math id="A6.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}_{t}-r_{t}=\Phi(p_{t})-r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}_{t}-r_{t}=\Phi(p_{t})-r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is accordingly the instantaneous interest rate change that would erase the arbitrageur’s gain: at the rate <math id="A6.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, funding payments would exactly offset financing costs, and the hedged position would earn no reward for convergence. The interest rate cost would cancel the gains from the initial price gap. As a result, the total payoff becomes zero under the instantaneous interest rate change.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2212.06888v7/fig_implied_rate.svg" id="A6.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/237;" width="476" height="237"></object></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure F.1: </span>Implied Interest Rates from Perpetual Futures Prices</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A6.F1.2" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel"><span id="A6.F1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">This figure presents the 7-day moving averages of the annualized implied interest rate <math id="A6.F1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> of Equation (<a href="#A6.E66" title="In Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">66</span></a>), the interest rate level at which observed perpetual futures and spot prices would be arbitrage-free, for the five cryptocurrencies. The dashed black line is the annualized DeFi financing rate.</span></p></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="A6.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p13.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F1" title="Figure F.1 ‣ Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a> plots the 7-day moving average of the implied interest rate for each of the five cryptocurrencies, together with the DeFi financing rate. The gap between the two is significant. The financing rate averages <math id="A6.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> per year, with a standard deviation of <math id="A6.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.6\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and remains between <math id="A6.p13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> throughout the sample. The implied rate, by contrast, swings between roughly <math id="A6.p13.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-200\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>200</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-200\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p13.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+400\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>400</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+400\%</annotation></semantics></math> per year in the early sample and remains far more volatile than the interest rate thereafter.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p14.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T2" title="Table F.2 ‣ Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a> summarizes the distribution of the implied interest rate <math id="A6.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>. Its standard deviation ranges from <math id="A6.p14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>62</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.p14.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="174\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>174</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">174\%</annotation></semantics></math> per year across currencies, orders of magnitude larger than the level of the interest rate itself. The implied rate is also negative in <math id="A6.p14.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.p14.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="34\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>34</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">34\%</annotation></semantics></math> of hours, a region a nonnegative financing rate cannot reach.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p15" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p15.1" class="ltx_p">These comparisons are unconditional. The next question is whether the required change is large relative to the interest rate risk prevailing at the moment. The distinction matters here because, as Figure <a href="#A1.F4" title="Figure A.4 ‣ Appendix A Additional Figures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a> shows, the volatility of the financing rate is itself far from constant.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table F.2: </span>Summary Statistics of Implied Interest Rates</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A6.T2.3" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel"><span id="A6.T2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">This table summarizes the annualized implied interest rate <math id="A6.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> of Equation (<a href="#A6.E66" title="In Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">66</span></a>), the level of the risk-free rate at which observed perpetual futures and spot prices would be arbitrage-free. Mean, Std, p5, and p95 describe the distribution of <math id="A6.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> over the hourly samples laid out in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.1 Data ‣ 4 Data and Empirical Analysis ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. <math id="A6.T2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;2\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;2\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> (%) and <math id="A6.T2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;6\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;6\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> (%) are the shares of hours in which the instantaneous rate change required to erase the arbitrageur’s gain exceeds two and six conditional standard deviations of the financing rate, <math id="A6.T2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|r^{*}_{t}-r_{t}\right|&gt;k\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|r^{*}_{t}-r_{t}\right|&gt;k\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A6.T2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.T2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=6</annotation></semantics></math>. The conditional volatility <math id="A6.T2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the residual standard deviation of the AR(1) of Equation (<a href="#A6.E69" title="In Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">69</span></a>).</span></p></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="A6.p16" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p16.1" class="ltx_p">We therefore estimate the conditional volatility of the financing rate from a rolling Vasicek fit. For each date <math id="A6.p16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we estimate the AR(1) regression</p>
<table id="A6.E69" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E69.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s+1}=a_{t}+b_{t}r_{s}+\varepsilon_{s+1},\qquad\varepsilon_{s+1}\sim\left(0,\sigma_{t}^{2}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s+1}=a_{t}+b_{t}r_{s}+\varepsilon_{s+1},\qquad\varepsilon_{s+1}\sim\left(0,\sigma_{t}^{2}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A6.p16.2" class="ltx_p">by OLS on the <math id="A6.p16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90</annotation></semantics></math> daily observations of the annualized financing rate strictly preceding <math id="A6.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and take the standard deviation of the fitted residuals, <math id="A6.p16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, as the conditional one-day volatility of the level of the rate. The procedure recovers the heteroskedasticity visible in Figure <a href="#A1.F4" title="Figure A.4 ‣ Appendix A Additional Figures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a>: the median <math id="A6.p16.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A6.p16.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points per year, but <math id="A6.p16.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> ranges from <math id="A6.p16.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.p16.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.7</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p17" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p17.1" class="ltx_p">The last two columns of Table <a href="#A6.T2" title="Table F.2 ‣ Appendix F Stochastic Interest Rates ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a> report the share of hours in which the required change exceeds two and six conditional standard deviations. The required change is beyond <math id="A6.p17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A6.p17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.p17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>92</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92\%</annotation></semantics></math> of hours and beyond <math id="A6.p17.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A6.p17.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="51\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>51</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">51\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.p17.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>68</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68\%</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p18" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p18.1" class="ltx_p">In sum, a stochastic short rate leaves the structure of the arbitrage payoff intact up to a small rebalancing term. The interest rate movements that would be required to rationalize observed deviations are implausibly large: they are frequently infeasible outright for defi rates, and where they are feasible they are routinely six or more conditional standard deviations of the prevailing financing rate. The evidence suggests that the deviation from our no-arbitrage benchmark is unlikely to come from stochastic interest rates.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>A Model of Deviations in Perpetual Futures</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Explaining Futures-spot Deviations ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> attributes the futures-spot deviation to the interaction between end users’ demand for leverage and the frictions faced by the arbitrageurs who accommodate it. This appendix uses the simple theoretical model to illustrate how these two forces influence the equilibrium deviation <math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>. The model delivers two predictions that guide our empirical analysis. First, greater arbitrage supply sensitivity and looser capital constraints would reduce equilibrium deviations. Second, the relationship between end-user demand and the deviation can be kinked: once arbitrage capital becomes constrained, each additional dollar of demand generates a larger deviation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Consider an environment with two groups of participants: end users, who demand leveraged exposure through perpetual futures, and arbitrageurs, who accommodate this demand by taking the opposite position and hedging in the spot market.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">End users.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">End users value the leverage provided by perpetual futures. For example, a trader who obtains one dollar of long exposure through the perpetual futures rather than purchasing the underlying token and financing the purchase in the cash market pays the deviation <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> per unit of time. Thus, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> can be interpreted as the price of obtaining leveraged exposure through the perpetual market. We model aggregate net demand for perpetual exposure as</p>
<table id="A7.E70" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E70.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{d}_{t}=\theta_{t}-\eta\rho_{t},\qquad\eta&gt;0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{d}_{t}=\theta_{t}-\eta\rho_{t},\qquad\eta&gt;0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is a demand shifter and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> captures the sensitivity of end-user demand to the deviation. In our empirical analysis, we proxy for shifts in <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> using past returns.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Arbitrageurs.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Arbitrageurs accommodate end-user demand by taking an opposite position in the perpetual with an offsetting position in the spot market, as in the strategies described in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Per dollar of intermediated notional, the trade earns the deviation <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> but is subject to several costs and constraints. The first cost is the marginal cost <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> of opening her position. There can be many forms of such cost, for example, the trading costs <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa c</annotation></semantics></math> which we study extensively, as well as the expected cost of exchange default.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Arbitrageurs may also face a fixed cost of entry, as studied by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bryzgalova et al. (2025)</a></cite>. Our model focuses on the equilibrium after the entry decision has been made.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Secondly, arbitrageurs bear the risk that the deviation widens before the position can be unwound in the perpetual market. Let <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the variance of the deviation per unit of time, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> the holding period, and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> the arbitrageur’s risk aversion. Under mean-variance preferences, an arbitrage position with notional <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> therefore entails a risk-bearing cost of <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{A}{2}X^{2}\sigma^{2}h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{A}{2}X^{2}\sigma^{2}h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Third, arbitrageurs face margin constraints. Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brunnermeier and Pedersen (2009)</a></cite>, let <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the capital available to arbitrageurs and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> the amount of margin required per dollar of intermediated notional. The position must then satisfy <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="mX\leq W_{t}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">mX\leq W_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Consider a positive deviation <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t}&gt;k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t}&gt;k</annotation></semantics></math>, so arbitrageurs have an incentive to enter the market. An arbitrageur chooses the size of the arbitrage position to solve:</p>
<table id="A7.E71" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.3" class="ltx_p">We refer to <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as arbitrage supply sensitivity, defined as the amount of notional that arbitrageurs are willing to intermediate per unit increase in the deviation when they are unconstrained. We refer to <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{W_{t}}{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mi>m</mi></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{W_{t}}{m}</annotation></semantics></math> as arbitrage capacity, the maximum amount of notional the arbitrageur can intermediate given the margin requirement.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The holding period <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is where the perpetual departs from a fixed-maturity contract. In a contract that expires at <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, convergence is guaranteed at delivery, and the horizon is capped at <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T-t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T-t</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded and known when the position is opened. In a perpetual, convergence occurs at a random time in the sense of Definition <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Definition 3 (Random-maturity arbitrage). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and the compensation accrues as a flow of funding payments rather than at a terminal date, so <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is random.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Equilibrium.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Setting <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{d}_{t}=X_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{d}_{t}=X_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> gives</p>
<table id="A7.E73" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E73.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t}=\frac{\theta_{t}+\Lambda_{t}k}{\eta+\Lambda_{t}}\quad\text{if capital constraint is slack},\qquad\rho_{t}=\frac{\theta_{t}-W_{t}/m}{\eta}\quad\text{if it binds}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>if capital constraint is slack</mtext><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>η</mi></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>if it binds</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t}=\frac{\theta_{t}+\Lambda_{t}k}{\eta+\Lambda_{t}}\quad\text{if capital constraint is slack},\qquad\rho_{t}=\frac{\theta_{t}-W_{t}/m}{\eta}\quad\text{if it binds}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(73)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Which branch applies depends on the state of end-user demand relative to available arbitrage capital. The capital constraint is slack when <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda_{t}(\rho_{t}-k)&lt;W_{t}/m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{t}(\rho_{t}-k)&lt;W_{t}/m</annotation></semantics></math>. Holding <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> fixed, this condition is satisfied for sufficiently low realizations of <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas high realizations cause the capital constraint to bind. The equilibrium deviation is therefore an increasing, kinked function of end-user demand: its sensitivity to <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> rises once arbitrage capital becomes constrained. This equilibrium characterization delivers two empirical predictions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Prediction 1: Greater arbitrage supply sensitivity and looser capital constraints reduce equilibrium deviations</h3>

<div id="A7.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the slack branch of Equation (<a href="#A7.E73" title="In Equilibrium. ‣ Appendix G A Model of Deviations in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">73</span></a>),</p>
<table id="A7.E74" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E74.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\Lambda_{t}}=\frac{k\eta-\theta_{t}}{\left(\eta+\Lambda_{t}\right)^{2}}&lt;0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\Lambda_{t}}=\frac{k\eta-\theta_{t}}{\left(\eta+\Lambda_{t}\right)^{2}}&lt;0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(74)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">since <math id="A7.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t}&gt;k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t}&gt;k</annotation></semantics></math> is equivalent to <math id="A7.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{t}&gt;k\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{t}&gt;k\eta</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="A7.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda_{t}\rightarrow\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{t}\rightarrow\infty</annotation></semantics></math> the equilibrium deviation approaches the cost floor <math id="A7.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, which is the no-arbitrage bound of Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition3" title="Proposition 3 (No-arbitrage bounds with trading costs). ‣ 3 Arbitrage in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>: with perfectly elastic arbitrage capital, the deviation collapses to the compensation for trading costs and venue risk. In the binding branch,</p>
<table id="A7.E75" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E75.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\left(W_{t}/m\right)}=-\frac{1}{\eta}&lt;0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>η</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\left(W_{t}/m\right)}=-\frac{1}{\eta}&lt;0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(75)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SSx1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so relaxing the margin requirement <math id="A7.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>, holding arbitrage capital <math id="A7.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> fixed, compresses the deviation directly.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Prediction 1: Arbitrage Constraints and Equilibrium Deviations ‣ 5 Explaining Futures-spot Deviations ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a> tests this prediction on Binance’s introduction of portfolio margining in April 2022, which allowed the spot and futures legs of the arbitrage to be collateralized inside a single account and therefore reduces <math id="A7.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>. The test provides evidence consistent with the model’s prediction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Prediction 2: Demand has a larger price impact when arbitrage capacity binds</h3>

<div id="A7.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Differentiating Equation (<a href="#A7.E73" title="In Equilibrium. ‣ Appendix G A Model of Deviations in Perpetual Futures ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">73</span></a>) with respect to the demand shifter gives</p>
<table id="A7.E76" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E76.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\theta_{t}}=\frac{1}{\eta+\Lambda_{t}}\quad\text{if capital constraint is slack},\qquad\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\theta_{t}}=\frac{1}{\eta}\quad\text{if it binds}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>if capital constraint is slack</mtext><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>η</mi></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>if it binds</mtext></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\theta_{t}}=\frac{1}{\eta+\Lambda_{t}}\quad\text{if capital constraint is slack},\qquad\frac{\partial\rho_{t}}{\partial\theta_{t}}=\frac{1}{\eta}\quad\text{if it binds},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(76)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and <math id="A7.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\eta&gt;1/(\eta+\Lambda_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\eta&gt;1/(\eta+\Lambda_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. When the constraint is slack, an increase in demand is partly absorbed by an expansion in arbitrage positions, dampening its effect on the deviation. Once the constraint binds, arbitrageurs can no longer expand their positions, so market clearing requires a larger adjustment in the deviation. The arbitrage supply curve is therefore kinked, with demand shocks producing larger price impacts in the constrained region.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The constrained region is also associated with larger equilibrium deviations, motivating the use of the initial deviation as an empirical proxy for proximity to the constrained regime.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Prediction 2: State Dependent Price Impact ‣ 5 Explaining Futures-spot Deviations ‣ Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a> takes this prediction to the data by estimating the price impact of perpetual order flow across different sizes of the initial premium index. Consistent with the model, order flow has a larger price impact when the initial deviation is larger, when arbitrage capital is more likely to be constrained. The evidence therefore supports the model’s prediction that capital constraints amplify the price impact of end-user demand.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
